name: RS-232 (DE-9 / DB9)
gender: male (DTE, e.g. a PC COM port)
description: The 9-pin serial connector on PCs and countless devices. Signal names are given from the DTE (terminal / PC) viewpoint: TXD is data the PC sends, RXD is data it receives. RS-232 signalling is bipolar (+/-3 to +/-15 V) and inverted, NOT TTL/3.3 V -- driving a bare MCU pin from it will damage it.

contacts.name: DCD
contacts.description: Data Carrier Detect (input to the DTE)

contacts.name: TXD
contacts.description: Transmit Data (out of the DTE / PC)

contacts.name: DTR
contacts.description: Data Terminal Ready (output from the DTE)

contacts.name: DSR
contacts.description: Data Set Ready (input to the DTE)

contacts.name: RTS
contacts.description: Request To Send (output from the DTE)

contacts.name: CTS
contacts.description: Clear To Send (input to the DTE)

variants: DE-9 (this) is the common 9-pin PC port; older equipment uses the 25-pin DB-25 with the same core signals plus rarely-used ones.
'DB9' is the near-universal misnomer: the D-sub shell for 9 pins is size E (so DE-9); 'DB' is the 25-pin shell size. Everyone says DB9 anyway.
DTE (PC) vs DCE (modem): on a DCE the data-direction names flip (its TXD is the DTE's RXD). A null-modem cable crosses the pairs to join two DTEs.
gotchas: RS-232 levels are bipolar +/-3 to +/-15 V and INVERTED (a mark/'1' is negative). This is NOT UART TTL -- connect it to a 3.3 V MCU only through a level shifter (MAX232 / MAX3232), or you fry the pin.
Names are from the DTE side. To talk to another DTE (two PCs, or a PC to a device also wired as DTE) you need a NULL-MODEM crossover: TXD<->RXD, RTS<->CTS, DTR<->DSR/DCD.
Minimum working cable is 3 wires: TXD (3), RXD (2), GND (5). Hardware flow control (RTS/CTS) is optional and many devices ignore it.
Pin 9 (RI) and pin 1 (DCD) are legacy modem lines -- usually left unconnected on non-modem gear.
notes: DE-9 (DB9) pinout from the DTE viewpoint per TIA/EIA-232. related max232 is the TTL<->RS-232 level shifter (already in partinfo); ft232rl/cp2102/ch340g are USB-serial bridges that expose these same logical signals at TTL level.
